TEXT
Online learning has grown enormously since students and teachers were forced to adapt during recent years. Today, many schools offer digital platforms where lessons, exercises and grades are all available with a single login. Supporters argue that this flexibility helps students who are ill, who live far from school, or who simply learn better at their own pace. Critics, however, warn that screens can never fully replace a real classroom, where students learn to interact, ask questions instantly and stay motivated by their peers. Most experts now agree that the ideal solution is a blend of both: technology used to support, not to replace, face-to-face teaching.

I. READING COMPREHENSION (6 marks)
1) According to the text, who benefits most from online learning?   (2 marks)
2) What is the main criticism made against online learning?   (2 marks)
3) What solution do most experts recommend?   (2 marks)

II. TEXT ANALYSIS (4 marks)
1) What is the writer's tone: alarmed, balanced, or mocking? Justify with one expression from the text.   (2 marks)
2) What is the writer's purpose in this text?   (2 marks)

III. LANGUAGE - PASSIVE VOICE (6 marks)
1) Put into the passive: "Many schools offer digital platforms."   (2 marks)
2) Put into the passive: "Students learn to interact in a real classroom."   (2 marks)
3) Complete with "must": Technology ______ (use) to support teaching, not to replace it.   (2 marks)

IV. WRITING - REPORT (4 marks)
Write a short formal report (about 100-120 words) on the use of digital platforms at your school. Include a Title, a brief Introduction, one Finding, and one Recommendation. Use a formal register.
